transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I'm having a really hard time at work. I'm a construction manager, and lately, every time I have to get near a scaffold, a roof edge, or any upper platform... my head just tells me I'm about to go over. It doesn't matter if I can clearly see the rails are in place and I know the setup is completely safe. I just feel like I'm going to fall.
Is your fear of falling limited to situations where you are near heights, or do you experience it in other situations as well?

No, it's pretty much just when I'm up high. If I'm on the ground, walking around the site, I'm completely fine. I don't worry about tripping or falling on a flat surface or anything like that. It really is just when I'm elevated.
Has this fear of being near heights affected your ability to perform your job as a construction manager?

Yeah, it really has. I mean, I’ve missed or delayed enough of my upper-level walk-throughs lately that my crews and the subcontractors have actually started questioning my calls. They notice I'm not up there checking things. And... well, it got bad enough that my employer’s insurance company pushed for an occupational health review, just because I wasn’t completing those key safety inspections. So, yeah, it's definitely making it hard to do my job right now.
When did you first start feeling this fear of being near heights?
It started about thirteen months ago. There was an accident on a stair tower at one of our sites, and... yeah, this whole thing has just been going on ever since then.
Is it the sight of the height that triggers your fear, or is it more about being in a position where you could potentially fall?

It's definitely about being in that position. Just looking up at a tall building from the street doesn't bother me at all. But... the second I step onto temporary stairs, or even just walk toward an open upper floor on the site, it hits me instantly. My chest tightens up, my hands get wet, and I feel like my legs might just lock up on me before I can make myself take another step.
Did the accident on the stair tower thirteen months ago involve you directly or someone you know?

No, it wasn't me directly. It was one of the subcontractors working on the site. I didn't really know him personally, but... I was right there when it happened. Just seeing it, I guess... well, that was enough.
Do you ever find yourself reliving the accident on the stair tower in your mind, like it's happening all over again?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I remember it, obviously, but... I don't feel like I'm right back there watching it happen again. It's not really the memory of it that gets me. It's just... when I actually have to go up on the scaffolding or the stairs myself now, that's what does it.
Do you feel anxious or nervous in situations that have nothing to do with heights?

No, not really. It's just the heights. Like, if I'm on the ground, dealing with the crew, handling the paperwork, or just going about my normal day off the site, I'm completely fine. I don't feel nervous or anxious at all. It's strictly when I have to go up high that I get that feeling.
Have you started avoiding activities or places outside of work because they involve heights?

No, not really. I mean, I don't really do much outside of work that involves heights anyway. I'm not a rock climber or anything. I just go home, hang out with my family, maybe do some yard work. None of that really involves being up high, so I haven't really had to avoid anything in my personal life. It's just the job site that's the problem.
Has this fear of heights affected your relationships with family or friends in any way?

No, not at all. I mean, my wife knows I've been having a hard time at the site, but... it doesn't really affect us at home. We're not exactly going to amusement parks or hiking up mountains or anything. So, no, my relationships with my family and friends are completely fine. It hasn't caused any problems there.
Have you felt like your fear of heights has affected your overall well-being or happiness outside of work?

No, I wouldn't say so. Once I'm off the clock and back on solid ground, I'm just... normal. It doesn't really weigh on me when I'm at home or on the weekends. I don't really think about it unless I know I have to go up high for a job. So, yeah, outside of work, my life and how I feel are pretty much fine.
Have you felt like your fear of heights has affected your self-esteem or overall sense of confidence outside of your job as a construction manager?

No, I don't think it has. I mean, like I said, when I'm not at work, I'm just my regular self. I don't feel bad about myself or anything just because I can't handle the scaffolding right now. It's frustrating, sure, because it's messing with my job, but it hasn't made me feel like less of a person or less confident in my day-to-day life. I still know who I am and what I'm capable of when I'm on the ground.
Have you felt like your fear of heights has affected any aspects of your life beyond your job as a construction manager?

No, honestly, it really hasn't. Like I've been saying, it's just the job. Once I'm off the site and away from the heights, everything else is just... normal. It doesn't bleed into my personal life or anything else I do.
Are there any situations or activities outside of work where you feel like your fear of heights might be causing you distress or problems?

No, not at all. I know we keep kind of circling back to this, but... no. I don't do anything in my free time that involves being up high anyway. I'm not going rock climbing or anything like that on the weekends. So, it really doesn't cause me any problems or distress outside of work. It's just the job.
Are there any areas in your life, besides work, where you feel like your fear is holding you back or causing problems?

I feel like we're kind of beating a dead horse here, doc. No, there really aren't. Like I've been saying, it's strictly a work thing. My home life, my friends, my day-to-day stuff... none of that is affected. It's just the scaffolding and the heights on the job site that are holding me back right now. Everything else is completely fine.
Are there any aspects of your personal life where you wish you could participate more, but your fear of heights holds you back?

Look, I don't mean to be difficult, but... no. I really don't. I'm not missing out on anything in my personal life because of this. I don't want to go skydiving, I don't want to ride rollercoasters. I'm perfectly happy keeping my feet on the ground when I'm off the clock. It's just the job site that's the issue.
Is your fear when you're in high places more about the possibility of falling or is it just being up high that bothers you?

It's the falling. That's exactly why I'm here, honestly. Every time I have to get near a scaffold, or a roof edge, or some upper platform now... my head just tells me I'm about to go over. And the frustrating part is, I can see the rails are in place. I know the setup is supposed to be safe, I know the regulations. But my brain just completely convinces me I'm going to fall off the edge anyway.
Would you feel anxious or uncomfortable if you were in a high place for a non-work-related reason, such as visiting an observation deck on a skyscraper?

I honestly couldn't tell you, because I just don't go to places like that. Like I said, I have absolutely no reason to visit an observation deck on my days off. If I was up there... I mean, maybe I'd feel that same panic about falling, but I really don't know. I just don't put myself in those kinds of situations to begin with, so it hasn't come up.
